..(Friday night through Wednesday)
Issued at 435 AM EDT THU JUL 30 2026

The main change to the grids for the first part of the extended 
forecast this morning was primarily to include more in the way of
PoP details and timing per the latest CAMs guidance on Saturday. 
It still looks like this next system is able to take advantage of 
increasing moisture pooling and a digging mid level trough
crossing into Kentucky this weekend to bring an increasing threat
for heavy rain - mainly on Saturday and Saturday night. The sfc 
pattern will feature a deepening and compact low pressure system  
rolling into the state on Saturday and Saturday night lifting and
concentrating the available moisture - yielding a potential for 
heavy to excessive rain. Expect the quick arrival of convection 
by midday Saturday to limit the instability that can build up so 
that only a small threat for organized or severe storms are 
anticipated despite semi-favorable wind shear working over the
CWA. 

The previous long term discussion follows:

The long-term period opens Friday morning with an upper-level trough
axis extending from Atlantic Canada southward along the Atlantic
Seaboard. Meanwhile, an ~588 dam high will be in place over 
Arizona and New Mexico with broad ridging extending to the north 
across the Canadian Prairies. Less prominent ridging extends east
and northeast from the high to across the Mid-Mississippi Valley,
Ohio Valley, and beyond into Southwest Quebec. A sharpening and 
digging upper-level shortwave trough is also sliding across the 
Upper Midwest through the eastern side of the ridge. At the 
surface, high pressure, centered over West Virginia, dominates the
the Central Appalachians and into adjacent regions. Meanwhile, 
low pressure is consolidating from Kansas to Iowa ahead of the 
shortwave trough (and will become our most significant weather 
maker of the forecast period).

The surface high pressure system and associated shortwave ridging
aloft will shift east to along the Atlantic Seaboard by the end 
of the day Friday while the deepening 500 hPa shortwave dives 
southeast and the attendant surface low tracks across the mid- 
Mississippi Valley, moving directly over the Commonwealth Saturday
night. Some of the energy within this trough will be captured by 
a broader 500 hPa trough pivoting through Eastern Canada and the 
Great Lakes. Guidance suggests whatever energy remains pinches off
into a closed low that then retrogrades toward the Lower Mississippi
Valley early next week and becomes entrapped under the eastward- 
building 500 hPa ridging. As a result, the surface low will 
occlude, sink southward, and decay on Monday. Meanwhile, a cold 
front associated with the trough passing through the Northeast 
will brush to our north and east.

As the low pressure system approaches, southerly flow will send PWATs
rising to 1.75+ inches (around 80th percentile relative to climo) on
Saturday, but those higher values will be short-lived overall as
drier air sinks back in from the north behind the retrograding low
and trough brushing to our north. WPC has a Marginal to Slight 
Risk for Excessive Rainfall over the JKL CWA on Saturday and 
Saturday night to account for the potential of locally heavy 
rainfall, which is the main concern in the long-term period. 
However, several days of antecedent drying as well as the overall
progressive nature of the system should help mitigate hydro 
concerns. Fortunately, the instability and shear parameter space 
remains weak and that should preclude any notable severe 
convective weather threat.

Sensibly, look for increasing clouds on Friday and Friday night with
high temperatures in the lower to mid 80s and low temperatures in
the lower to middle 60s. Rain chances return on Saturday and peak
at categorical PoPs Saturday night and early Sunday morning. 
Daily rain chances follow for Monday through Wednesday, but 
convective coverage should be more sparse and modulated by the 
diurnal heating cycle. Temperatures will continue to run in the 
lower to middle 80s for highs each afternoon (except upper 70s for
some locations on Sunday), while nighttime lows dip into the 65 
to 70 degree range for most.
